preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer N (1 ≤ N ≤ 100000) representing the number of engineers.
The input consists of exactly N + 1 lines: the first line is N, followed by N lines of desk assignments.
Each of the N subsequent lines contains exactly two integers: current desk and desired desk.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(current) <= 2 * N and 1 <= int(desired) <= 2 * N for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for current, desired in [line.split()])
preconditions.description: Each desk number (current and desired) is between 1 and 2*N inclusive.

preconditions.expression: len({int(line.split()[0]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]}) == N
preconditions.description: No two engineers currently sit at the same desk (all current desks are unique).

postconditions.description: The output is a non-negative integer modulo 1000000007 (10^9 + 7).

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(current) <= 2 * N and 1 <= int(desired) <= 2 * N for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:] for current, desired in [line.split()])
postconditions.description: The output is the count of valid seating arrangements where each engineer either stays at their current desk or moves to their desired desk, with no two engineers sharing the same desk in the new arrangement.

postconditions.expression: int(stdout.strip()) == len([assignment for assignment in product(*[set([int(line.split()[0]), int(line.split()[1])]) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]]) if len(set(assignment)) == N]) % 1000000007
postconditions.description: The output is computed as the number of valid assignments (each engineer assigned to either their current or desired desk) with all desks unique, modulo 1000000007. The assignment is a tuple of length N where each element is either the current or desired desk of the corresponding engineer.
